defs_parts: Four labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: A Godot node maps to a Unity GameObject and an Unreal Actor.
Edit the template and copies follow, but an override keeps its own value.
A Blueprint graph is binary, so an agent cannot diff it as text.
Godot's fixed step runs sixty times a second, Unity's FixedUpdate fifty.
A Godot mask works one way, and an Unreal response needs both sides.
Godot and Unity are Y-up in metres, and Unreal is Z-up in centimetres.
bookends.segment: Name The Term In Each Engine
bookends.command: Quiz me on porting a Godot game to Unity and Unreal, with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms GameObject, Actor, Prefab, override, ScriptableObject, Event Dispatcher, FixedUpdate, Layer Collision Matrix, Object Type and Z-up. For each case I must name the exact term in the right engine and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply.
checks: Check: each case names the engine, and the answer waits for your reply.
Check: you gave the exact engine term and said why the look-alike fails.
